result.body:
Found while fixing #387 part 2.

`src/culturemech/import/mediadb_importer.py:37` carries a hardcoded patch:

```python
# The first four rows in the archived MediaDB compound export are corrupted
...
    "preferred_term": "Water",
    "kegg_compound": "C00001",
```

...for compound ids 1-4 (Water, ATP, NAD+, NADH).

The rows were not corrupt in the source. `mediadb_fetcher.py` read the
`compounds` columns in the wrong order — the dump's schema is
`compID | KEGG_ID | BiGG_ID | name | seed_id | pubchem_ids | chebi_ids | formula`,
and the parser took `parts[1]` as the name (that is KEGG_ID) and `parts[3]`
(the real name) as the ChEBI id. Row 1 came out as `name='C00001'`,
`chebi_id='Water'`, which is what someone saw and patched by hand.

#387's fix corrects the mapping. Re-parsing the same dump now gives:

```
1: 'Water' kegg='C00001'
2: 'ATP'   kegg='C00002'
3: 'NAD+'  kegg='C00003'
4: 'NADH'  kegg='C00004'
```

— exactly what the patch hardcodes, so it is now a no-op.

## Why it was not removed there

`data/raw/mediadb/mediadb_compounds.json` is gitignored. A checkout with a
stale copy, generated before the parser fix, still has the shifted fields, and
for those four rows the patch is the only thing standing between that file and
four wrong ingredient names. Removing it in the same PR would have made the fix
depend on everyone re-fetching.

## Suggested

Remove the hardcode once the export is regenerated, and consider having the
importer *detect* the shifted shape (e.g. a `name` that looks like a KEGG id,
`C\d{5}`) and refuse, rather than silently patching four rows of it. The patch
only ever covered 4 of the 14,797 compounds; the other 14,793 were shifted too
and nobody noticed.

comments.body:
Partly addressed in \`041de781a2\` on #391 — the *detection* half of the
suggestion, not the hardcode removal.

Measured while reviewing #391: the `mediadb_compounds.json` on this machine
still held **1,703 truncated rows and 14,695 shifted ones**. So the risk was
not theoretical — `just import-mediadb` without a re-fetch would have put
`'Iron(III` back into the corpus, and could have introduced damage from the
~1,600 fragments that never reached a recipe the first time.

The importer now refuses a pre-fix export rather than silently patching four
rows of it:

```
regenerated (correct)    ACCEPTED, 14797 compounds
pre-fix backup (stale)   REFUSED, 14695 shifted / 1703 truncated
```

Worth recording that the first version of the guard was wrong in the direction
that matters. It counted any `name` matching `C\d{5}` and refused the
*correctly* regenerated export, because four MediaDB compounds are genuinely
unnamed and carry their KEGG id as the name — `{'name': 'C15810', 'kegg_id':
'C15810'}` is real data. Under the shifted mapping the two columns disagree
(`{'name': 'C00149', 'kegg_id': 'mal-L'}`), and that disagreement is the actual
signal. Only testing the negative case caught it.

**Still open here:** removing the four-row hardcode itself. The guard makes
that safe to do — a stale export can no longer reach the importer — but it is a
separate change and this PR is already large.

result.title: mediadb_importer hardcodes four compounds to work around a parser bug that is now fixed
